# Build decisions log

Choices builders made where mvp-spec.md v1.4 is silent, ambiguous or contradictory (pick, log, keep going). Logan signs them off at the milestone gates. A value chosen here is a named constant in code, with a comment pointing back to its row.

| Id | Spec | Question | Choice | Constant | PR | Signed off |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | 5.13, 5.14, 5.17 | The sector table with annual volatility, beta and typical payout ratio is in no CSV; `g_sector` is undefined | One shared default per value for all 42 industries (all industries already share defaults); `g_sector` is the industry's `lt` growth | `SECTOR_VOLATILITY`, `SECTOR_BETA`, `SECTOR_PAYOUT` (set in M5/M6) | Phase 0 | Logan, plan |
| D2 | all | Tie-break when the spec gives none | Lower id wins, so iteration order stays deterministic | (none) | Phase 0 | Logan, plan |
| D3 | 3 | Share counts as u32 overflow for large companies | Share counts are u64; money is f64 USD, with CSV $M, $bn and bps converted once at load | (none) | Phase 0 | Logan, plan |
| D4 | 3, 9.2 | What order are table ordinals (province, company, industry and the rest) in? | Ascending byte order of the CSV id (CO-0001 is CompanyId 0); rows born in play append. Ties to the lower id (D2) are ties to the lower ordinal | (none) | M1 | |
| D5 | 4.1 step 1, 9.1 | 4.1 applies queued controls at the start of a tick, but while paused no tick runs, so a queued Resume would never apply | `Sim::apply` applies controls at once. MVP controls change only runner state (speed, pause, skip, alerts, watchlist), never the world, so this equals applying them at the next tick's step 1 | (none) | M1 | |
| D6 | 4.1 step 4, 8 | When do alerts fire, and does a Pause alert stop a SkipTo? | Calendar alerts (Earnings day, Plan lock, Quarterly recap) fire in 4.1 step 4; alerts raised by later jobs (bankruptcy, world event) fire where raised; a Pause alert pauses after its tick. During a SkipTo, Pause alerts only notify, so the skip stops at its target. The alert notice carries its level; Off posts nothing | `AlertKind::default_level` | M1 | |
| D7 | 4.4, 8, 21.8 | How is days_to_next_phase counted, and how long is the Release phase? | Calendar days from today to the day the next phase starts. Release is the 00:00 tick only (Reaction starts 01:00), so the release tick reads 0 | `RELEASE_DAY`, `PRICE_MOVE_HOUR`, `PLAN_LOCK_DAY`, `RECAP_DAYS_BEFORE_RELEASE` | M1 | |
| D8 | 3.1, 7.3, 9.1 | Speed model and SkipTo targets | Speeds 1 to 5 run at 2 s, 1 s, 0.5 s and 0.2 s of real time per game hour and max (spec 8). A new game is paused at speed 1. SetSpeed(0) pauses; SetSpeed(1 to 5) sets the speed and resumes; Pause and Resume keep the speed; Pause or SetSpeed cancels a skip. SkipTo resumes at max speed and pauses after the first target tick strictly after now: NextRelease and NextLock the next release and lock ticks, NextRecap the next pre-quarter-end week start, MonthEnd the next 1st at 00:00 (the tick that closes the month) | `START_SPEED`, `MAX_SPEED`, `SECONDS_PER_HOUR` | M1 | |
| D9 | 3.1, 12.3 | How each RNG stream is seeded from the game seed | One ChaCha8 key from `seed_from_u64(seed)`; the streams differ by ChaCha stream number, frozen: cycle 0, growth 1, prices 2, ai 3, gen 4. Box-Muller keeps its second normal as a saved spare. Knuth's Poisson is used up to a mean of 30 | `Stream` discriminants, `POISSON_MAX_MEAN` | M1 | |
| D10 | 9.3 | Which day, month or quarter do the notices name? | DayDone the day just ended; MonthDone the month just closed; EarningsReleased the quarter just ended (2 Jan 2020 is Q4 2019); PlanLocked the calendar quarter the lock falls in. TickDone is always the last notice of a step | (none) | M1 | |
| D11 | 2.1, 3.7.2, 9.2 | Spec 2.1 says to load only the characters named as controller or owner_of_record, but 9.2 `list_characters` lists all 296: the two contradict (design fix 11) | All 296 characters load into the character table; the named-controller role is a later field | (none) | M1 | |
| D12 | 4, 7.3 | Does the first step run the 2020-01-01 00:00 jobs? | No. A tick advances the clock, then runs the jobs for the new time, so the first tick is 01:00 on 1 January 2020; the 00:00 start state is built at load (7.3: plans set and the Q1 draw made at load) | `DateTime::START` | M1 | |
| D13 | 9.1, build-plan 4.3 | What does a save hold, what does the hash cover, and what happens on load? | A save holds the whole world (static tables too, so it loads without the CSVs), the RNG positions and the controls. The state hash covers the world and the RNG positions, not the controls (they never change the world). Loading pauses the game and drops any skip; Omniscient is cleared in release builds | `SAVE_VERSION`, `HASH_FORMAT` | M1 | |
| D14 | build-plan M0.8, M7.7 | The table spike's real-GPU checks (frame time, wheel step, HiDPI clicks, resize, fonts, 10,000 rows) could not be run by screen control | Folded into M7.7: the table widget logs frame and sort times to stdout in release, and its tests cover pool sizing on resize and a 10,000-row sort; Logan checks wheel feel and HiDPI clicks by hand at the M6 + M7 gate | (none) | housekeeping | |
| D100 | 4.3 step 2, 5.1, 5.3 | 4.3 step 1 draws the new quarter before step 2 moves demand, and the 1 Jan 2020 job never runs (D12): whose growth moves the month, and does Q1 2020 lose a third? | The monthly job closes the month just ended, so demand_core, trend_demand and the fringe move by the growth and lt of the quarter that month belongs to: on a quarter's first day (after step 1) that is last quarter's prev_q_growth and prev_lt. Each quarter's growth lands over the jobs on its 2nd and 3rd month and the next quarter's 1st; Q1 2020 loses nothing, and demand after each 1 January job is validate.py's year-end demand. Labels still read this quarter's q_growth | `demand::closing_rates`, `Industry::prev_lt` | M2 | |
| D101 | 5.1 | Phase lengths: whole or continuous quarters? How is g drawn? | Whole quarters, uniform inclusive (validate.py's randint); `quarters_left` counts the current quarter, so a phase drawn at 24 runs 24 quarters. g = lo + (hi − lo) × u from one cycle-stream uniform, with Contraction and Recovery written low to high as validate.py draws them. Draw order on entering a phase: g, then the length | `cycle::phase_spec`, `cycle::START_PHASE` | M2 | |
| D102 | 5.1 | own_shock_sd is "3% a year": convert it to a quarterly sd? | No conversion: the shock is added to the zone effect, which is itself a yearly rate (intensity × g_t), and a fresh shock replaces the last each quarter (it does not accumulate), so own_shock_sd is the sd of each quarter's draw. z is a cycle-stream normal clamped to ±3 like the growth shock, drawn after the cycle advances, in zone id order, only for zones with own_shock_sd above 0 (Cuba, North Korea and Russia, design fix 101), also at load | `cycle::NORMAL_CLAMP` | M2 | |
| D103 | 5.1.1 | The boom sets linked industries' prev_q_growth to the new lt_q; the pop says only "prev_q_growth resets". Which industries, and how without losing last quarter's growth? | Both reset only industries with boom_uplift above 0 (the others' lt does not move, so a reset would only erase their cycle gap; validate.py resets all, which is the same in its noise-free run). The reset is a flag the next draw reads (it carries over from lt_q), so prev_q_growth still holds last quarter's real growth for step 2 (D100) and screens. No reset at boom-year changes or at the bust's end. The pop cuts every industry's demand_core and trend_demand by crash_drop, not the fringe (5.1.1 Supply: S jumps). The World event alert fires at the boom and at the pop | `Industry::carry_reset` | M2 | |
| D104 | 5.1, 5.1.1 | Order of the label rules against the boom override; Glut's exit rule | The 5.1.1 forced Boom (first 4 boom quarters) and Bust (8 bust quarters) of linked industries win over every 5.1 rule. Otherwise first match: Bust at gap ≤ −5%; Glut when last month's S > 1.15, or the label was Glut and S ≥ 1.10; Boom at gap ≥ +5%; Normal | `LABEL_GAP`, `GLUT_ENTER_S`, `GLUT_EXIT_S`, `BOOM_LABEL_QUARTERS` | M2 | |
| D105 | 5.10, 6 | Order inside 4.3 step 11, when growth tranches age, and the plan before the Lite AI exists | Decay first (capacity at cost, book by the same amount capped at the book, ramping tranches by the same share), then tranches age, then the plan buys or sells sized on the gross before this month's decay, so g = 0 buys back the decay exactly. A growth tranche counts at 80% for the next 6 month closes. Sales take the same share of the book and of ramping tranches. Step 11 records capex, sale proceeds and gain on the unit; cash moves at the 4.3 step 13 settle (M4). Until the M6 plan lock every unit runs g = 0 and R&D at rd_norm | `RAMP_SHORTFALL`, `RAMP_MONTHS`, `SALE_FACTOR_*`, `PLACEHOLDER_GROWTH_PLAN`, `assets::placeholder_plan` | M2 | |
| D106 | 7.1, 5.8 | Which PC bonus does load use? The 7.1 "iterate twice" rule does not settle for CO-0154, CO-0540 and CO-0651 (~$42B each): the station rule on their loaded gross assets gives +6, but company-start.csv was generated at +5 (design fix 201, lane F) | Load sets Company::pc_bonus by the 7.1 two-pass rule from companies.csv revenue, the value the data was generated with, so every unit makes its companies.csv revenue at M 1.0 (worst 0.0001% off). Productivity stations at load round halves to even, as gen.py's Python round does. M3's monthly compute step (4.3 step 5) owns the bonus from the first month on | `start::start_pc_bonus`, `LOAD_STATION_SHARE` | M2 | |
| D107 | 7.1, build-plan M2.6 | CO-0003, CO-0026 and CO-0027 have revenue 0, so no unit can match companies.csv within 0.5% | Companies under $0.1M take the barebones loadout ($100,000 of assets, PC bonus +1) and make $101,000 a year; the M2.6 check covers the other 648 | `BAREBONES_REVENUE_USD`, `BAREBONES_GROSS_USD` | M2 | |
| D108 | 5.5, 3.8, 7.1 | Shared costs (3.8 compute) are M3.5, but the fixed cost rate at load subtracts them | M2 counts shared costs as 0 at load and monthly (two named hooks, to be filled together in M3.5), so the fixed cost rate at load is f × turnover − d_eff: 0.441 to 0.45, not the spec's 0.38 to 0.449, and fixed cash carries the whole fixed share. Break-even at productivity 100 and M 1.0 holds either way | `start::shared_costs_at_load_hook`, `revenue::shared_costs_month_hook` | M2 | |
| D109 | 5.1.2 | How is the effective spread rounded? | To whole bps, half away from zero, after the clamp; stored as a fraction (D3) | `SPREAD_CYCLE_K`, `SPREAD_MIN_MULT`, `SPREAD_MAX_MULT` | M2 | |
| D110 | 7.2, 7.3 | What does load compute beyond the draws? | Fringe from companies.csv revenue (7.2); supply, S and M; labels from the Q1 2020 draw and the load S; and each unit's month of revenue and expenses at the load M (a run-rate month, for the views and M4's synthetic history). S at load is 1.00 to two decimals, not exactly 1, since gross assets are whole dollars and the barebones three make $101,000 | (none) | M2 | |
| D111 | 5.1.1 | Stage arithmetic and the tipped lab | The AI stage is read from quarter counts: Boom from the boom quarter to the pop quarter, Bust for 8 quarters, then Postcrash; the boom year is whole years into the boom, the last ai-boom.csv row holding after. The pop roll is the first gen-stream draws at load (year offset, then quarter). The tipped lab (drawn at load only to name the headline) is left to the M6 news work and will draw after the pop roll | `BOOM_YEAR`, `POP_BASE_YEAR`, `POP_YEAR_ROLL`, `POP_QUARTERS`, `BUST_QUARTERS` | M2 | |
| D112 | 3.4, 8, 9.2 | Industry `published` snapshot and the 20-quarter chart | No published copy: the industry views rebuild only at the monthly close, so they already show the month just closed. Each industry keeps its last 20 closed quarters (demand, supply, growth, lt), added at 4.3 step 6 on a quarter's first day. `get_cycle` shows the pop date only in Omniscient | `supply::HISTORY_QUARTERS` | M2 | |
